chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hajjaj from Thal'abah ibn Zayd from Burayd said:
I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the fresh dates (ruthab) being sold in two or three portions (qita'), he said, 'There is no harm in it.'
He said, So I increased my questioning about similar matters, and he would say, 'There is no harm in it.'
So I said, 'May Allah rectify you, indeed those among us are corrupting this entirely for us.'
He said, 'I think they heard the hadith of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) regarding the palms.'
Then a man interposed between me and him, so he fell silent.
So I commanded Muhammad ibn Muslim to ask Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the saying of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) regarding the palms.
Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said, 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) went out and heard a noise/clamor, so he said, "What is this?"'
It was said, "The people are trading in the palms," so the palms were held back (not sold) this year.'
So he (peace be upon him and his family) said, "When they do that, do not buy the palms until something appears in them and is not yet prohibited (by drying out)."'

key_terms.الرَّطْبَة: Fresh dates, partially ripened dates still on the tree
key_terms.فَعَلُوا: They did (referring to the practice of holding back palms)
key_terms.قِطْعَة: A portion or share, often implying a sale of a specific part of a crop
key_terms.يَطْلُعَ فِيهِ شَيْءٌ: Something appears in it (referring to the emergence of fruit)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to sell fresh dates in portions according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) clarifies that selling fresh dates in portions is valid, distinguishing it from the specific prohibition of 'holding back' palms (tadhrir) to manipulate market prices, a practice the Prophet warned against due to its negative impact on the tree's yield. This ruling underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on separating general commercial permissibility from specific market manipulations, ensuring transactions are based on clear, observable qualities rather than speculative delays.
